reference: Olkiluoto, Finland, crystalline bedrock (no published log for these boxes)

description.lithology: Two rows show the same rock - upper row is a long continuous piece with a short detached piece in the lower row, representing one drilling run. Rock is a light grey to off-white and medium grey, medium-grained, foliated to gneissic veined gneiss / migmatitic gneiss of granitic to tonalitic composition. Heterogeneous texture with irregular leucocratic quartz-feldspar domains/patches and darker biotite-rich foliated bands defining a moderately to well developed gneissic foliation/banding at low angle to sub-parallel to the core axis. No sharp lithological contact visible in the imaged interval.
description.alteration: none visible - no obvious oxidation, chloritic, sericitic, silicified or carbonate alteration distinguishable at this resolution; dark bands appear to be primary mafic foliation/biotite rather than alteration. Red line is a drill orientation mark, not geology.
description.mineralization: none visible - no discernible sulfide or ore minerals such as pyrite, chalcopyrite, pyrrhotite, sphalerite or galena visible at available resolution; no disseminated, veinlet, bleb or massive style observed.

anomalies.explanation: A single sub-transverse fracture/break is visible in the upper row about 75-80% from the left, with no visible fault gouge, infill or offset at this resolution.

Irregular leucocratic quartz-feldspar patches and diffuse veinlets/neosome throughout the core give a migmatitic/veined fabric that should be checked in hand specimen to distinguish from discrete veins.
Lower row contains a short detached core fragment of the same lithology, reflecting tray layout for a single run, not a different lithology.
